dimensions.note: CredentialInputSchema.secret is .meta({sensitive:true}) and is supplied via vault.get(). The new gitlab-pat probe passes it only as a PRIVATE-TOKEN request header; it is never logged, never written to a resource, and never included in the detail string. Only the id, expiry and status leave the method. Mechanical check: neither the credential nor the audit resource payload contains a secret-bearing field.
Unchanged by this revision. All logging remains in the audit method: one structured info line per credential and a completion line, with no secret on any path.

preflight() throws before any probe runs, refusing the whole audit on duplicate or colliding ids — a partial audit reporting success is the silent under-count this model exists to prevent. The gitlab-pat probe never throws: network failure, unexpected status and unparseable JSON each map to a distinct status (unreachable) with the cause in detail, so one unreachable endpoint cannot abort the audit of every other credential. HTTP status codes are carried into detail.

29 tests over mocked fetch, 10 new for this change. Failure and edge paths covered: 401, 403 insufficient_scope, absent expires_at, revoked-with-future-expiry, network throw, already-lapsed, trailing-slash base URL, and a test asserting probeFor covers every declared PROBE_KIND. No live calls.

Read-only by construction — no create, delete or mutating method exists, so there is no already-exists or already-gone case and re-running is inherently safe. A partially completed run leaves no external state; the only side effect is resource writes, and preflight refuses the run before any of them if the configuration could under-count.

The endpoint (GET /api/v4/personal_access_tokens/self) and the 401-vs-403 distinction were both verified against live GitLab documentation during this change: 403 insufficient_scope is documented for a valid token lacking scope, and 401 for invalid or missing authentication. Response fields are read defensively with typeof guards; a non-JSON 2xx body is caught and reported as unreachable rather than throwing. No pagination applies — the self endpoint returns a single object. AbortSignal.timeout bounds the request.

No file handles, sockets or temp files; fetch only, with AbortSignal.timeout on every request including the new probe. The model creates no external resources, so there is nothing to track for later cleanup.

Re-reviewed for this revision, which adds five new code examples to the README. All use fictional or documentation values: gitlab.example.com, github.example.com, the credential ids connect-token/deploy-bot, pat/dependency-sweep and gitlab/mirror-sync, and a generic vault named store. No IPv4 literals, internal hostnames, CIDRs, real project paths or account identifiers in any shipped file.

CredentialSchema and AuditSchema are plain z.object with no .passthrough(). Widening PROBE_KINDS extends the kind enum in place, so the declared shape stays exact and CEL expression validation continues to resolve attributes.
Unchanged by this revision: credential and audit both carry lifetime infinite with garbageCollection 30, which retains a month of daily audit history.

Not a CRUD lifecycle model. It is a read-only prober with a single audit method and deliberately no create, update, delete or sync — that absence is the property that makes it safe to run unattended against production credentials, and is stated in the module docs. Lifecycle management for GitLab tokens lives in @sntxrr/gitlab-token.

The dimension covers pre-flight checks on mutating methods; this model has none to guard. It nonetheless validates before acting: preflight() runs at the top of audit and throws on duplicate ids or ids that normalise to the same resource name, refusing the entire run rather than silently overwriting one credential's result with another's. A swamp checks block would not auto-fire here in any case, since checks trigger only on methods named create/update/delete/action.

Each credential is keyed by resourceNameFor(id), which normalises manifest-shaped ids like connect-token/deploy-bot into a safe instance name, and preflight refuses the run if two distinct ids would collide after normalisation — so no credential can silently overwrite another. The audit summary is a deliberate singleton keyed current: it is a per-run report, not a managed external resource, so the real-ID convention does not apply to it.

dataRepository is never accessed directly and no method reads back stored state. Every probe reads the credential the consumer actually holds — the deliberate design choice recorded in the module docs — rather than a prior snapshot, so a deployment left on a superseded credential surfaces as its own finding.

No upgrades entry is required for 2026.08.19.3 to 2026.08.19.4. This revision changes documentation only: README prose and examples, plus JSDoc on four exported symbols (ProbeKind, Status, Logger, model). No schema, field, argument or runtime behaviour changed, so there is nothing to migrate.
